title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The handwriting is on the back of a typed page of the SGA 3 Exposé XIII typescript on Cartan subgroups and the scheme of maximal tori. It has nothing to do with that text. It is scratch work on zero-cycles and the Albanese variety of a product.

1. Set-up. X and Y are varieties with base points a ∈ X and b ∈ Y, and Z = X×Y. A is an abelian variety with group law A×A→A.

2. Products of degree-zero cycles. For zero-cycles z on X and z' on Y with z~0 and z'~0 (degree zero, or algebraically equivalent to 0), he forms (z×b)×(a×z') in Z×Z = X×Y×X×Y. He compares it with (z×z')×(b×a), which suggests a symmetry or shuffle argument on Z×Z.

3. Albanese of a product. A general zero-cycle on Z is written Σ u_{x,y}(x,y). He writes the natural maps Alb(X)×Alb(Y) → Alb(X×Y) and Alb(X×Y)^τ → Alb(X)^τ×Alb(Y)^τ, where τ probably denotes a torsor or a twisted/ordinary version. For an abelian variety A he checks that A → Alb(A)^τ is 'bien injectif', 'bien surjectif', hence bijective. Crossed-out identities (gα)α' = g etc. are routine checks of a group action, presumably the torsor structure.

4. The key computation at the bottom. With φ the Albanese map:
- the point (x,y) goes to (φ(x)−φ(a), φ(y)−φ(b));
- the cycle (x,y) − (x,b) − (a,y) + (a,b) = (x−a)×(y−b) has image zero in Alb(X×Y) = Alb X × Alb Y;
- the line 'x − x − a + a' checks the degenerate case y = b.
So exterior products of degree-zero cycles lie in the Albanese kernel T(X×Y).

5. Filtration on zero-cycles. The line '(,S)X/(,S)_2X ≠ (,S)X/_2X' seems to compare quotients of the group of zero-cycles (or of a related functor) by a second filtration step. This would be an F^1/F^2-type filtration in which F^2 should contain products like those above.

6. A logic chart. A boxed diagram reads [2,2bis,3,3bis] ⇔ [4,4bis] ⇒ [5], with [6,6bis] and 5° below, '3 ⇒ 4', crossed-out 'th. de Weil', 'via les conditions' and a '?' arrow back. It records the logical dependencies among numbered conditions or statements on another page. These could be characterisations of the Albanese by a universal property, or conjectural statements about cycles in the cote's theme (Hodge/Tate/Lefschetz/Weil). Weil's theorem was evidently meant as an input, then struck out.

Purpose: understanding the structure of zero-cycles modulo rational/algebraic equivalence on products, i.e. the Albanese map and its kernel. This is the theme later made central by Mumford (1969), Roitman, Bloch and Beilinson.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. Alb(X×Y) ≅ Alb(X)×Alb(Y) for pointed varieties, and (x−a)×(y−b) ↦ 0 in the Albanese, are both correct.
The page is too fragmentary to check the numbered implications [2..6bis], since their content is on another page.

ideas.what: Albanese of a product: Alb(X)×Alb(Y) ≅ Alb(X×Y), with point (x,y) ↦ (φ(x)−φ(a), φ(y)−φ(b))
ideas.where_published: Albanese in FGA/Bourbaki seminars context (Picard scheme duality); not specifically this computation

ideas.what: The exterior product (x−a)×(y−b) = (x,y)−(x,b)−(a,y)+(a,b) of degree-zero cycles maps to zero in Alb(X×Y), i.e. lies in the Albanese kernel
ideas.modern_name: Products of degree-zero cycles lie in F^2 of the Bloch–Beilinson filtration / Albanese kernel T(X×Y)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bloch (1970s, Lectures on algebraic cycles 1980); Mumford 1969 for nontriviality of the Albanese kernel

ideas.what: Comparing quotients of zero-cycles by successive filtration steps ('(,S)X/(,S)_2X ≠ ...')
ideas.modern_name: Filtration on CH_0 (F^1 = degree-zero part, F^2 = Albanese kernel)

ideas.what: Chart of logical implications among numbered conditions [2,2bis,3,3bis] ⇔ [4,4bis] ⇒ [5], [6,6bis], with 'th. de Weil' struck out
ideas.modern_name: Unclear: possibly equivalences among characterisations of the Albanese or among cycle-theoretic conjectures

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly computes that products of degree-zero zero-cycles on X and Y die in Alb(X×Y). He also appears to compare a second filtration step on zero-cycles of X×Y. Together this is an early (1965–71) look at what became the Albanese kernel and the F^2 step of the Bloch–Beilinson filtration. It is not developed further here.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It shows Grothendieck considering the structure of CH_0 beyond the Albanese in the context of the standard conjectures, before Bloch's work. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: These are scratch computations on the Albanese of a product and on degree-zero cycle products, all now standard. The only mildly interesting point is the early hint of a filtration on zero-cycles, and it is too fragmentary to claim anything substantive.
transcription_corrections: The handwriting is unrelated to the typed SGA 3 Exp. XIII text underneath (back side or reuse of a typescript page).
'𝔷' is most likely an ordinary handwritten z or ζ denoting a zero-cycle; 'z ~ 0', 'z' ~ 0' are the degree-zero conditions.
The superscript on 'Alb(A)^τ' is uncertain; it may be τ or a similar symbol.
The words read 'bien injectif' / 'bien surjectif' are uncertain; together they assert A → Alb(A) bijective.
'Σ A_i(x,b)' is crossed out and replaced by 'Σ u_{x,y}(x,y)', a general zero-cycle on X×Y.
The bottom line 'x − x − a + a' is the specialisation y = b of (x,y)−(x,b)−(a,y)+(a,b).
